# everpure_azure_volume_group_status (Data Source)

Reads the status of an existing Volume Group: its space usage and how many hosts its volumes are connected to.

The values can be used in any condition Terraform evaluates. In a [`check` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/checks), a failed assertion is reported as a warning during plan and apply, and the run continues. In a `precondition` or `postcondition`, a failed condition stops the run.

`max_connected_hosts_per_volume` is the largest number of hosts any single volume in the group is connected to, not the number of distinct hosts: two volumes each connected to a different host read `1`. It counts configured connections, not active iSCSI sessions, so it does not change when a guest logs out. Space values are in bytes.

If the volume group cannot be read, the read fails with the service's error. Inside a `check` block that error is reported as a warning.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

# Looks up a Volume Group and the Storage Pool it lives on.
data "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  name                = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
}

data "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
}

# In a check block, a failed assert is reported as a warning during plan and apply, and
# the run continues.
check "volume_group_status" {
  data "everpure_azure_volume_group_status" "example" {
    volume_group_id = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  }

  assert {
    condition     = coalesce(data.everpure_azure_volume_group_status.example.max_connected_hosts_per_volume, 0) > 0
    error_message = "Volume group is not connected to any host."
  }

  # The service sets no limit on a volume group's space; this threshold (1 TiB) is
  # your own.
  assert {
    condition     = try(data.everpure_azure_volume_group_status.example.space.total_used_in_bytes, 0) < 1099511627776
    error_message = "Volume group uses more than 1 TiB."
  }
}

# In a precondition, a failed condition stops the run. The status is read outside a
# check block here.
data "everpure_azure_volume_group_status" "gate" {
  volume_group_id = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
}

resource "terraform_data" "require_volume_group_headroom" {
  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = try(data.everpure_azure_volume_group_status.gate.space.total_used_in_bytes, 0) < 1099511627776
      error_message = "Volume group uses more than 1 TiB."
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the Volume Group. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `max_connected_hosts_per_volume` (Number) The largest number of hosts any single volume in the group is connected to. It counts configured connections, not active iSCSI sessions, so it does not change when a guest logs out. 0 for a group with no volumes.
- `space` (Attributes) Space usage, in bytes. Null when the service reports none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--space))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the volume group's status.


<a id="nestedatt--space"></a>
### Nested Schema for `space`

Read-Only:

- `shared_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by duplicated data, meaning data shared among different volumes and snapshots as a result of data deduplication, in bytes.
- `snapshots_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by data unique to one or more snapshots, in bytes.
- `total_used_in_bytes` (Number) Total space occupied by customer data, in bytes. This is the space being billed for.
- `unique_in_bytes` (Number) Unique space occupied by customer data, in bytes.
